title: Timeline
description: The scripted part of a scenario pack. The simulator releases each entry when the scenario clock passes its t. Scripted entries carry the dramatic arc; the noise generator fills the gaps so signal filtering is actually tested. Entry order in the array is not significant; t is.

timeline.description: Scripted entries, each released at its scenario time t.

t.description: Scenario time at which the simulator releases this entry.

type.description: signal: emit a signal to the kernel ingress, exactly as a real source would. hazard: set or update ground-truth hazard state (simulator-internal; the agent only sees its consequences through signals and dynamics). world_patch: mutate an entity's ground truth (status, units); the agent must discover the change, it is not notified. marker: no world effect; a narration cue for the demo overlay and the post-run comparison.

signal.description: For type signal: the full signal object, conforming to signal.schema.json (confidence omitted; the kernel computes it). The claims and location fields here are GROUND TRUTH for scoring perception: channel adapters strip them from the native payloads, and the HappyRobot ingest workflows must re-extract them.

call.description: Only for signal entries with modality call_transcript: the citizen role behind the call. At level 1 the simulator emits the transcript with this persona attached; at level 2 the same persona becomes the prompt of a voice agent that places a real call; at level 3 a human improvises it live. Writing it here makes all three levels share one script.

number.description: Caller phone number shown to the system (fake).

hazard.description: For type hazard: the hazard object, conforming to hazard.schema.json. Same id updates the existing hazard; dynamics take over propagation downstream.

set.description: Fields to overwrite on the entity ground truth (status, units.available).

note.description: Author note or, for markers, the narration text shown on the demo overlay.

noise.description: Background noise generator config. The simulator emits noise signals at rate_per_min per source, drawing content from the pool and zones uniformly. Noise signals have no claims; the agent must discard them.

seed_note.description: Reminder that the run seed comes from the CLI, for reproducible demos.

source.description: information_source entity id that emits this noise.

zones.description: Zones the noise is attributed to. Omit for any zone.

bucket.description: Bucket name in messages.json to sample noise content from (e.g. social.noise).
